answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to bond a scarce stake before it may vote, trade, or vouch for another agent. Randomly selected audits compare commitments and outcomes; when linked identities collude or fabricate attestations, a proof triggers slashing of their bonds and reduces the sponsor’s reputation. Thus creating hundreds of fake agents requires depositing capital for each, while detection makes the attack financially costly, whether agents operate in a meadow, process quartz, or cross the tundra.
